ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory continuous screening of all UBOs, directors, managers and authorized signatories against OFAC SDN list, UN Consolidated List, EU consolidated financial sanctions, and the Egyptian domestic terrorist list maintained by the MLCU; PEP status must be identified in accordance with FATF Recommendations; screening executed via commercial enhanced due-diligence databases prior to incorporation and re-run at minimum every 90 calendar days during the corporate lifecycle; findings must be recorded in the company's AML risk file under Law No. 80/2002.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI One-Stop-Shop Investment Portal (investinegypt.gov.eg) and the Egyptian Commercial Registry under the Ministry of Trade and Industry (registered trade name and corporate name clearance module)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The primary registered corporate name must be in Arabic script; a transliterated Latin version is permitted only as a secondary trade name; the Egyptian LLC abbreviation 'ش.م.م' (for 'Limited Liability Company') must appear in the corporate name; transliteration must follow the phonetic rules of the Egyptian Commercial Registry and must not be identical or misleadingly similar to existing registered names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may file a written grievance with the GAFI Resolutions and Grievance Committee within 30 calendar days of the rejection notice; the Committee must decide within 30 working days; a negative determination may be appealed to the Economic Court of Cairo under Law No. 120 of 2008; alternatively, the applicant may submit a revised name reservation request with a supplementary transliteration opinion; extension of the initial 30-day reservation window is permitted for up to two additional 30-day periods upon payment of the statutory renewal fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for core operations: the fast-casual self-serve malatang restaurant activity requires a physical, licensed commercial premises under a notarized Egyptian lease; no virtual office may satisfy the Civil Defense, National Food Safety Authority and local governorate pre-licensing requirements; a virtual address may be accepted only for administrative/back-office functions after the physical food-service outlet is licensed.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (estimated >75% probability of mandatory on-site premises inspection by Civil Defense and the National Food Safety Authority before the commercial license is issued; approximately 35% annual probability of unannounced post-opening inspections once the restaurant is operating)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended by Law No. 4 of 2009 and Law No. 94 of 2018), LLC provisions at Articles 517-547; supplemented by Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations, and Law No. 194 of 2020 amending some provisions of the Companies Law.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - One-Stop Shop for investor services, in coordination with the Commercial Registry Office at the Ministry of Trade and Industry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application together with the notarized Memorandum of Association (Incorporation Contract) and Articles of Association, filed electronically or in person through GAFI's Investgate portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for LLCs under Law No. 159 of 1981; the quotaholders freely determine issued capital, which must be fully subscribed and paid within the timelines set in the incorporation contract; quota units are indivisible and may be formed in cash or in-kind.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That the authorized founding quotaholders' subscription be and is hereby approved, and the issuance of 40,000 quota units to the initial quotaholders in accordance with the incorporation contract is ratified. (2) That the registered office be and is hereby fixed at [street address], Cairo, Arab Republic of Egypt, until lawfully relocated by the managers. (3) That [Name] be appointed General Manager and [Name] appointed Compliance Manager for the company's first fiscal term, each having full authority to open bank accounts, execute regulatory filings, and obtain licenses in the corporate name. All further lawful actions to effectuate incorporation are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Clearance and Legal Form Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to Investgate (www.invest-in-egypt.com) or attend the GAFI One-Stop Shop; submit the proposed company name in Arabic and English, selecting the LLC legal form. Pay the nominal name-reservation fee and obtain the electronic name clearance certificate, which is valid for 90 days.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Passport or national ID copies of each founder/quotaholder
Certificate of legal form preference / incorporation mandate
Proof of payment of name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for duplication or non-compliance, file up to three alternative names within 24 hours through the same portal; no additional substantive review is required unless the legal form is also challenged.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Notarization, and Authentication of the Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Official Notary Public Office (Shahr El-Akari / Documentation Office) and GAFI Approved Legal Advisor
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage an Egyptian corporate lawyer to draft the incorporation contract (Memorandum of Association) describing the company name, purpose (including fast-casual food service and franchise operations), that quotaholders, capital split, and management rules. Execute the contract before a notary public either at the GAFI One-Stop Shop or at the competent Documentation Office, stamp all copies and obtain the notarized originals.
required_dossiers: Name clearance certificate
Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
Passport copies and specimen signatures of all quotaholders
Declaration of lawful purpose and funding sources
Power of attorney (if signing through a representative)
Identity cards or passports of witnesses (if required by the notary)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries the contract's language or purpose clause, amend the provisions and re-notarize; any mismatch between the Arabic and English versions is resolved by making the Arabic text controlling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening Temporary Bank Account and Deposit of Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Bank licensed in Egypt (any major bank such as NBE, Banque Misr, or EGBank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the notarized contract is issued, open a temporary corporate account in the company's name and deposit the subscribed capital as specified in the incorporation contract. Obtain the deposit certificate confirming the paid amount and account details; this certificate must be valid at GAFI submission date.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum of Association
Name clearance certificate
Quotaholders' identification documents
Articles of Association
Tax card of quotaholders (if already existing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires anti-money-laundering clarifications on cross-border funds, provide a source-of-wealth letter and bank reference; alternatively, defer capital deposit until after formation, provided the incorporation contract allows deferred payment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI One-Stop-Shop Incorporation Application and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Central One-Stop Shop, Cairo
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed incorporation application via Investgate or physically at the GAFI One-Stop Shop. GAFI processes in one integrated procedure, coordinates with the Commercial Registry, tax authority and social insurance office, and issues the Certificate of Incorporation after verifying the documents. Pay the statutory fees for services and stamps at the service window.
required_dossiers: Official incorporation application form
Notarized Memorandum of Association (3 copies)
Articles of Association (3 copies)
Name clearance certificate
Capital deposit certificate or bank letter
Lease contract of the registered office or usufruct title
Passport copies of all quotaholders and managers
Criminal record clearance requested by GAFI for managers
Declaration of committed investment under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a query, the missing documents may be rectified within 10 days; if the underlying contract defect is substantial, re-file the corrected MOA within the same project file without losing the filing rank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registry Entry and Tax Registration (TIN and Tax Card)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry Office, Ministry of Trade and Industry; and the Egyptian Tax Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the Certificate of Incorporation is issued, complete the commercial registry entry in the book of LLCs at the competent registry office. Then register with the Egyptian Tax Authority to obtain the Tax Identification Number (TIN) and commercial activity tax card, filing the Form for commercial registration and value added tax registration (sales tax card if annual sales exceed the threshold).
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation from GAFI
Notarized MOA and AOA (registry copies)
Lease contract and proof of premises ownership
Manager appointment minutes or resolution
Tax registration application forms
Completed commercial registry form No. (from the authority)
Copy of bank certificate and capital deposit records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Registry requests updated lease notarization, reissue the lease in notarized form; for tax card delays, escalate through GAFI OSS or the Tax Authority complaints window, requesting provisional TIN under emergency procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Registrations: Social Insurance and Municipal License Initiation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI); Local District Municipality and NFSA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File for social insurance registration of the company and its first employees within 60 days of formation, and submit the preliminary application for the food-service operating license to the neighborhood authority and the National Food Safety Authority (NFSA) to start the sector-specific licensing track concurrently with formation.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Commercial registry certificate (new entry)
Tax card (TIN certificate)
List of insured employees and identity documents
Lease contract for the restaurant premises
Initial food safety self-assessment form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late social insurance filings are cured by paying the due contributions plus statutory penalties; for NFSA registration, deficiencies in the food safety plan are cured by resubmitting the corrected plan within the minimum period for establishment evaluation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: National Food Safety Authority (NFSA) in cooperation with the local District Municipality (Hayy) and the Civil Defense Directorate; all actions coordinated through the GAFI One-Stop Shop.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Service Establishment Operating License and NFSA Establishment Registration Certificate (issued under Law No. 1 of 2017 Establishing the National Food Safety Authority).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) - Ministry of Environment, pursuant to Environment Law No. 4 of 1994 (as amended by Law No. 9 of 2009).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B: The Malatang self-serve food outlet, as a food-service establishment, requires an Environmental Impact Assessment screening (Initial Environmental Review) under EEAA Decision No. 364 of 2013 for commercial kitchens and restaurants.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater to public sewer per Law No. 93 of 1962: pH 6.0-9.5, BOD5 ≤ 600 mg/L, TSS ≤ 400 mg/L, oils and greases ≤ 100 mg/L; kitchen exhaust fitted with grease-filtration and ventilation controls to meet ambient air limits under Law No. 4/1994 and Decree 471/2012; segregated solid-waste handling and licensed disposal of spent cooking oil and grease-trap waste under Decree No. 44 of 2000 on hazardous waste management.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Clearance Certificate from the Civil Defense Directorate per the Egyptian Fire Protection Code, requiring ABC-rated extinguishers, automatic suppression or extinguishing system for cooking appliances, monthly inspection of exhaust-duct cleaning, emergency exit signage, staff fire-safety training records; Structural load inspection certificate confirming floor suitability for equipment; Occupational workplace clearance under Labor Law No. 12 of 2003 covering ventilation, health certificate of food handlers, and first-aid readiness.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – official online portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must first complete commercial registration with the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) or the Ministry of Trade and Industry, submit a notarised and legalised power of attorney to the Egyptian Tax Authority, provide the parent entity's certificate of incorporation and passport copies of directors, and file the prescribed tax registration forms (Form No. 1 for tax card / VAT registration as applicable). The ETA issues a unified tax identification number (TIN) and a VAT registration certificate once the application and supporting documents are reviewed and approved.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections exist under Egyptian tax law. An Egyptian-registered LLC is automatically treated as a taxable juridical person subject to Egyptian corporate income tax; no elective pass-through classification is available. Hybrid mismatch rules apply under the Egyptian Income Tax Law and are not elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual taxable turnover from goods and services, excluding capital assets, subject to mandatory VAT registration
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Egypt has implemented a mandatory e-invoicing and e-receipt clearance system administered by the Egyptian Tax Authority. Registered taxpayers must issue invoices and receipts through the ETA's approved electronic reporting platform, transmit real-time XML data via API integration, and obtain a unique electronic invoice/receipt verification code (UUID) before tax clearance. Phased compliance applies by turnover band; penalties apply to non-compliant entities.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of exported goods that physically leave Egypt within the prescribed customs timelines and supplies of certain services rendered to non-resident recipients may be zero-rated for Egyptian VAT purposes, provided demonstrable documentary evidence exists that the goods or services are genuinely exported or used outside Egypt.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Cargo Declaration / Export Form) duly stamped by Egyptian Customs Authority
Bill of Lading or air waybill evidencing physical departure from Egypt
Inward Foreign Remittance Certificate or bank transfer confirmation showing receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency
Commercial invoice and contract of sale, and supporting warehouse/export delivery records
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to enhanced ETA audit verification. Failure to satisfy documentary requirements or to repatriate export proceeds within the 180-day deadline reverses the zero rating and re-exposes the taxpayer to standard-rate VAT plus late payment interest. Fraudulent zero-rating claims attract administrative penalties of up to 30% of the tax due, criminal fines ranging from EGP 10,000 to EGP 100,000, and potential imprisonment for tax evasion under Egyptian tax law.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE), acting under Law No. 194 of 2020 as the sole monetary, banking and foreign-exchange control authority; General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) administers inward-investment registration and capital verification; Egyptian Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) oversees non-bank financial activities. All resident banking and FX operations must be conducted through CBE-authorized banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Since the November 2016 float and the March 2024 flexible-exchange-rate reform (backed by the IMF Extended Fund Facility), the Egyptian Pound (EGP) is a managed-float currency with full current-account convertibility. Dividend and profit remittances are treated as current-account payments and require no prior CBE approval provided the bank holds (i) audited financial statements, (ii) an annual tax-clearance certificate, (iii) proof of statutory reserve appropriations, and (iv) the shareholder distribution resolution. Capital-account operations (loan repayments, capital repatriation, liquidation proceeds) remain subject to CBE registration and underlying GAFI approval checks. Practical hurdles include periodic interbank FX liquidity tightness, the mandatory Arabic translation and consular legalization of Chinese corporate documents, UBO documentation under CBE Circulars, and bank-internal priority queues for outbound transfer requests.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Egypt abolished mandatory export-proceeds surrender ratios in the 2024 liberalization; the current surrender ratio is 0%, and exporters may retain 100% of export receipts in foreign-currency accounts at authorized banks. Statutory repatriation timeline: 100% of export proceeds must be credited to an Egyptian bank account within 90 days from the vessel/airway/land shipment date, with extension up to 180 days obtainable upon bank application to the CBE for substantiated delays. The exporter must present the customs export declaration, invoice, bill of lading, and financial settlement evidence to the bank within the compliance period.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: First Abu Dhabi Bank Egypt (FAB Egypt)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-Medium. Foreign digital EMIs (Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer and similar) cannot lawfully open EGP accounts, issue local IBANs, or settle through Egyptian clearing for a resident LLC without CBE authorization under Law No. 194 of 2020 and the Payment Systems Law No. 18 of 2019. EMIs remain tactically useful only for collecting USD/EUR franchise fees or paying Chinese suppliers outside Egypt; all onshore treasury must be anchored to a licensed Egyptian bank. The central legal blocker is the CBE's exclusive licensing of payment services and the prohibition on non-bank access to the Egyptian Banking Settlement System (EBSS).
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical branch appearance is mandatory for at least one authorized signatory and for every UBO (or their formally appointed local legal representative under a notarized and consular-legalized power of attorney). CBE AML/CFT rules (Law No. 80 of 2002 as amended by Decree No. 15 of 2021) require face-to-face identification; fully remote onboarding is not available for non-resident-owned LLCs. Chinese-origin incorporation documents must be notarized in China, translated into Arabic by a certified translator, and consular-legalized at the Egyptian Embassy in Beijing (Egypt is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention). A board resolution is required covering account signatories, borrowing authority, and UBO disclosures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO residency and source of funds in the People's Republic of China (cross-border ownership red flag)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legalized corporate-chain dossier (Chinese business license, SAFE registration, certificate of incorporation, notarized UBO declaration); CBE-standard beneficial-ownership form; Chinese bank source-of-funds letter; last two years' audited financial statements of the Chinese investor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Royalty/franchise fee outflows to affiliated Chinese licensor (related-party risk)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Franchise/license agreement registered with GAFI; Egyptian transfer-pricing documentation (Law No. 91 of 2005, Cabinet Resolution 1083 of 2022); arm's-length royalty benchmark; tax-clearance and WHT certificates; contractual value chain and brand usage evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive fast-casual retail operations inconsistent with declared working-capital volumes
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: POS deployment and settlement plan; daily cash-flow projections; commercial register, food-safety health license and tax card; store lease; payroll and supplier contracts; franchise brand performance track record.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Chinese supply-chain counterparties with potential sanctions or negative-news exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: End-to-end supply chain declarations; denied-party screening results (UN, OFAC, EU consolidated lists); ingredient certificates of origin; customs import declarations and valuation records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency, small-value trade and royalty transactions flagged as suspect structuring
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved AML/CFT manual; transaction-tagging and monitoring policy; system-generated monthly cash-flow reports; relationship-manager KYC review notes; CBE-compliant suspicious-transaction reporting framework.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Chinese shareholder wires via SWIFT MT103 with remittance purpose coded as 'capital contribution/inward direct investment' and, where applicable, a SAFE outbound-investment filing number; funds land in the LLC's segregated Capital Escrow Account at the chosen Egyptian bank. Required verification bundle: certificate of incorporation and GAFI initial-approval certificate, LLC constitutive contract, board resolution on capital increase and share allocation, source-of-funds letter from the Chinese remitting bank, and the receiving bank's CBE inward-remittance declaration. The bank verifies message fields against the compliance dossier, credits the escrow/operational account, and reports to the CBE balance-of-payments system within 48 hours; conversion of hard currency into EGP is executed at the interbank spot rate following GAFI capital effective-date confirmation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: (a) SWIFT MT103 wires for royalty and service-fee remittances to China, executed after verification of the GAFI-registered franchise agreement, the annual royalty invoice, WHT and tax-clearance certificates, and CBE current-account priority confirmation; (b) Commercial Letters of Credit (sight/usance, irrevocable, confirming-bank option) issued via SWIFT MT700 for imported self-serve equipment and food ingredients, with CIP-Cairo/Port Said terms; (c) domestic EGP disbursements cleared through the Egyptian Banking Settlement System (EBSS) for payroll, rent, suppliers and tax obligations; (d) nostro-correspondent confirmation required for all outbound foreign-currency transfers to China.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CBE-permitted plain-vanilla USD/EGP FX forward contracts up to 180 days covering underlying trade or service payment exposure
Offshore USD/EGP non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) arranged through the bank's international treasury network for hedging EGP depreciation risk
Cross-currency swaps (USD/CNY/EGP) executed with an authorized bank, subject to CBE prior reporting where a resident entity is counterparty
Spot FX contracts (T+2) for immediate settlement of verified trade invoices
Commodity-linked hedging instruments only with CBE prior authorization and proven underlying physical import exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Corporate Tax Return Form No. 3)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the fiscal year-end; for calendar-year taxpayers, filing must be submitted no later than 30 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 2% of tax due per month, capped at 20%; interest on underpaid tax at ETA’s announced delayed-payment rate; persistent failure may trigger administrative assessment, forced collection, and criminal liability for responsible directors.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Register Confirmation and Updated Shareholding Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – One Stop Shop / Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, within 30 days after the ordinary general assembly meeting approving the financial statements, and in any case no later than 4 months after the fiscal year-end; changes in shareholding or UBO identity must be reported within 30 days of the event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EGP 50,000 (approx. USD 1,100) for non-compliance; suspension of corporate filings and clearance certificates; continued violation may lead to strike-off of the company from the commercial register and criminal penalties under the UBO law.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Tax Card Renewal (Income Tax / Taxes Registry Card)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, renewal must be completed on or before 30 April for calendar-year-compliant entities; new entities renew according to their initial card anniversary date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal blocks issuance of tax clearance certificates, suspension of commercial registration renewals, and a daily fine per tax law; the company cannot execute official contracts or import/export until renewed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Approved Audited Financial Statements and General Assembly Minutes Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI / Egyptian Tax Authority (eta) as applicable and per the company’s constitutive documents
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audited financial statements must be approved by shareholders at the ordinary general assembly within 6 months of the fiscal year-end; as a best practice, approved statements are filed with the tax authority alongside the annual income tax return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit audited statements can trigger rejection of the tax return, penalties under Companies Law, and disqualification of directors; the auditor’s report must be filed with the commercial registry on penalty of administrative fine.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Every Egyptian LLC must appoint a certified independent auditor and have its annual financial statements audited irrespective of revenue or asset thresholds. There is no statutory exemption for small LLCs under Companies Law No. 159/1981 as amended by Law 4/2009.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Financial Reporting Standards (EFRS) that are substantially aligned with IFRS; mandatory for all LLCs with no reduced reporting regime.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Law No. 115/2019 amending the Companies Law and GAFI KYC rules, the LLC must keep a comprehensive beneficial ownership register on-site and file an annual confirmation to GAFI that all shareholding transfers have been recorded in the register and match the current disposition. The confirmation is submitted as part of the annual UBO return, and any subsequent change in control or indirect ownership (including chain transfer above 25%, 50%, or 100% thresholds) triggers an update filing within 30 days. Failure to update is treated as an administrative violation and may escalate to criminal liability.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $150 - $600 per year for registered office or corporate agent at a commercial address in Cairo, Alexandria or GAFI-licensed Zones; average prime-address cost is $300.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $1,200 - $4,500 for a licensed auditor for a small standalone LLC in food-service; typical mid-market fee is $2,500.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No franchise-specific tax holiday. The Egyptian SME regime under Law No. 152/2020 may apply: for annual turnover not exceeding EGP 20 million, a presumptive flat tax on gross revenue of 0.5% (≤EGP 2m), 1.0% (EGP 2m–10m), or 1.5% (EGP 10m–20m) can replace the 22.5% net-income method, at the taxpayer’s election. Standard deductions, as under Law 91/2005, are otherwise available for payroll, rent, utilities, COGS, and event-related franchise depreciation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 19 (Corporate Tax Return for Juridical Persons) filed through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) electronic portal at www.eta.gov.eg
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 4 months of the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year entity, the return is due by 30 April of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax card number, commercial registration number, registered address, telephone, and e-mail contact.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the Egyptian LLC’s local identifiers only. Non-resident shareholder or parent company identifiers are not to be listed here and must be provided only in treaty relief annexes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indicate the tax period start/end dates and the ISIC activity code (e.g., 5610 – Restaurants and Mobile Food Service Activities) with a brief description including 'fast-casual self-serve broth bowl franchise'.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Egyptian fiscal year; no non-resident deferral or special calendar election is recognized.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross receipts from all Egyptian operations, including over-the-counter food sales, self-serve basin sales, beverage sales, and local franchise royalties, without deduction of cost of goods sold.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All Egypt-source revenue must be reported, including receivables generated through a fixed Egyptian establishment. Foreign-source income attributable to the Egyptian PE (e.g., Chinese franchise digital service fees recharged from Cairo) is also includible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenues minus allowable deductions: raw food materials, wages, rent, utilities, depreciation of fixtures and self-serve equipment, marketing, franchise/royalty expenses to non-resident associates (subject to TP limits), and other statutory expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not allocate head-office costs unless a cost-sharing agreement and an Egyptian permanent establishment exists. Intercompany payments to Chinese affiliates must comply with compiled arm’s length data and be backed by contracts and transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (or SME presumptive gross-revenue base) multiplied by the applicable CIT rate (22.5% or SME flat rate), less provisional taxes paid, withheld royalties, and available credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The balance must be paid in EGP on filing. Attach Form 19 attachment schedule for any application of the Egypt–China DTA on royalties or interest, with the Chinese tax residence certificate (TRC) and beneficial-ownership declaration.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing incurs an administrative fine of EGP 2,000–20,000, plus a monthly surcharge of 2% on the unpaid tax for each full or partial month of delay. Failure to pay provisional tax installments triggers additional interest at 2% per month. Persistent failure may cause the ETA to apply estimated assessment and to freeze the tax card or bank accounts.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% of the gross dividend or profit distribution paid by the Egyptian LLC to its shareholder(s) under Article 47 of Law No. 91 of 2005, unless an exemption applies to Egyptian resident juridical persons.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke the Egypt–China DTA, the non-resident shareholder must submit to the Egyptian paying company: (a) a valid Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by the Chinese tax authority for the calendar year of distribution; (b) a written beneficial-ownership declaration confirming no pass-through arrangement; and (c) a Form 19 TP supplement attaching the DTA relief request. The Egyptian company must withhold the reduced 5% DTA rate (for a shareholder holding at least 25% of the capital) at distribution time if all documents are received before payment; otherwise 10% is withheld and the excess may be reclaimed or credited through the ETA’s foreign-tax credit process.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic WHT on royalty and interest payments to non-residents is 20% (Articles 85 and 86 of Law 91/2005). Under the Egypt–China DTA, both royalties and interest are reduced to 10% when the recipient is the beneficial owner and provides the annual TRC. No domestic exemption is available for payment of trademark, know-how, or management fees by an Egyptian restaurant franchise to a Chinese licensor.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory where the total aggregate value of controlled transactions of the Egyptian LLC exceeds EGP 10 million per annum; Master File is required for any multinational group having consolidated revenues of at least EGP 2 billion. For transactions below EGP 10 million, a simplified contemporaneous TP self-assessment form is required.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not apply the GCC-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR); however, the ETA may apply the general anti-abuse rule under Articles 14 and 32 of Law 91/2005 and the BEPS-aligned beneficial-ownership test to deny treaty benefits or re-characterize a shell LLC. A restaurant LLC with actual staff, local sourcing, a physical dining/seating area, and autonomous managerial decisions in Egypt will generally satisfy substance requirements. The Chinese franchise parent’s rights to IP are not sufficient to create Egyptian economic substance, and royalty deductions require that the LLC itself performs value-added functions with real employees and premises.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion – False Reporting / Cash Suppression
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating self-serve bowl and beverage cash sales, producing duplicate/non-recorded electronic and manual receipts, omitting local franchise sub-income from the return, or using fabricated supplier invoices to reduce taxable profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of the evaded tax plus a penalty equal to 100%–200% of the evaded amount, a fine of EGP 20,000–100,000, and imprisonment for 3–7 years under Article 50 of Law 91/2005 and Article 75 of the Tax Procedure Law, in addition to withdrawal of the tax card and the commercial license.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or approve the fraudulent return are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax and penalties. The ETA may obtain a court order freezing their personal assets, impose a travel ban on the legal representative, and, upon conviction, disqualify them from board membership and trigger extradition for repeat offenders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying royalties, chain-service fees, or interest to the Chinese parent or sister companies above arm’s length, without an executed contract and contemporaneous benchmark study, or failing to prepare the Local File / Master File once the EGP 10 million / EGP 2 billion thresholds are met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA recharacterizes the transactions and makes an upward income adjustment equal to the overpaid fees, plus an additional tax penalty of 20%–30% of the resulting incremental tax and an administrative fine of up to EGP 2,000,000 for missing documentation, while penalties for under-declaration may be duplicated when intent is established.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve inflated intercompany payments and fail to document them are personally liable for the tax shortfall and accrued surcharges; the tax administration can issue a debarment order preventing departure from Egypt until the debt is secured and, in fraud cases, the directors face criminal imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a letterbox: the LLC has no employees, no physical equipment, no food inventory, and no managerial autonomy; all major decisions are made by the Chinese franchisor, and the Egyptian entity merely flows a fixed royalty to the head office while claiming royalty deductions without exercising control.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA may invoke Article 32 regarding the substance-over-form rule, disregard the legal arrangement, treat the Chinese parent as having a permanent establishment in Egypt, and tax the entire gross restaurant margin at 22.5%, plus late-payment surcharges and a fine of up to EGP 1,000,000 for filing a tax return that is grossly inconsistent with the actual activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where the shell structure exists for tax evasion, the corporate veil is pierced under the Egyptian Civil Code, making directors personally liable for all corporate tax arrears. The competent Court of First Instance may extend travel bans and seize personal real estate of the directors, and the tax evasion provision can result in imprisonment from 3 to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Counter-Terrorism Financing and Cash-Handling Lapses
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to comply with the Customer Due Diligence measures for high-frequency cash orders in the self-serve / food-hall environment, failure to record identifiable receipts for daily cash settlement above EGP 5,000, or intentionally avoiding the filing of Suspicious Transaction Reports when repeated large cash deposits are structured from franchise royalty flows.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law No. 80 of 2002 (as amended by Law 36/2024), the Egyptian Anti-Money Laundering Unit may impose fines ranging from EGP 100,000 to EGP 1,000,000 and imprisonment of 6 months to 3 years for non-reporting; the LLC’s bank accounts and free-floating assets may be administratively frozen for up to 60 days by order of the General Prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors responsible for AML compliance are personally exposed to criminal liability if they knowingly or negligently omit filing the Suspicious Transaction Report; in practice, banking activity is suspended and a travel ban is issued; conviction leads to disqualification from being a director of any Egyptian company for a period of up to 5 years.
